name: plan_extract
description: How vpt/plan_extract.py finds storeys, room labels, room outlines, walls and doors in a DXF, and how tools/export_plan.py draws each storey. Every value is a starting value: check it against your drawing (the export prints the checks R1-R5 with three outcomes).
layer_regex_note: Layer names <storey>_<nn>_[Abbruch_|Neubau_]<base> (the toolkit's convention, presets/synthetic_flat.json). Layers that do not match (e.g. 0, Defpoints) belong to no storey; when no layer matches at all, the whole drawing is one storey with key 'all' and every layer's base is its own name.
exclude_status_note: Layers of these statuses (walls to demolish) are left out of room labels, outlines, walls and doors. They are still drawn in the SVG.
label_area_regex_note: A label line matching this is the room's area text; the first other line is the room's name.
text_reader_note: plain = ezdxf's fast plain_text() (enough for the synthetic flat). mtext_clean = for drawings from a DWG converter: ezdxf's full MTEXT parser, which reads the non-breaking space \~ inside formatting (the fast reader drops the code and what follows it, so an area line such as '5,00\~m{...}' is not recognised), after repairing a size value without its leading zero (\H.66x;); then the caret of a stacked superscript is dropped ('m2^' -> 'm2') and spaces are collapsed.

room_label_rule.note: every_text = every text on a room-label layer with a name line is a room (its area line, or the nearest lone area text within three text heights, is its area). area_with_name_above = only an area text (label_area_regex matching at its start) makes a room: its name is the nearest single-line text directly above it (left edges within max_dx_heights text heights, top at most max_dy_heights higher), or the line above the area line of one multi-line MTEXT; the room's anchor is the area text. Use it when the label layer also holds notes, finishes, heights or dimensions. table_header_regex (empty = none, e.g. '^TOP\b') marks the header of a table on the label layer; texts in its window (from one header height left of its left edge to table_window_right_heights to the right, down to table_window_down_heights below its top) are never labels. Distances in text heights of the area text (table: of the header).

wall_reader.note: exploded_lines = the LINE and LWPOLYLINE pieces on the wall layers, block content included (straight polyline pieces only). top_level_paths = every top-level entity on the wall layers (lines, polylines with their arcs, arcs, circles, splines and HATCH boundaries, flattened within flatten_m), block content left out: use it when walls are drawn as hatches, or when blocks on the wall layers are details or symbols rather than walls (their pieces would otherwise count as walls between a point and a room label).

label_max_dist_m_note: A point outside every outline belongs to the nearest room label within this distance whose straight line to the point crosses no wall segment.

doors.note: A door is an ARC on a door layer with radius in radius_m (the leaf width) and sweep in sweep_deg. Hinge = the arc centre. Closed end of the arc (the opening): the end with NO line from the hinge when exactly one end has one (within leaf_tol_m; that line is the open leaf), else the only end that touches a wall segment (within leaf_tol_m: the far edge of the opening, where the wall goes on), else the end whose direction from the hinge runs along (within wall_angle_tol_deg) a wall segment of at least wall_min_len_m within wall_search_m of the hinge, else could not tell. Rooms on both sides: probe points from the middle of the opening along and against the open leaf at the side_probe_m distances (the first that finds a room wins). Two leaves whose closed ends lie within double_tol_m are a pair (double door).

windows.note: A window is a group of straight lines on a window layer: lines of at least min_width_m running in the same direction (within parallel_deg) whose extents along it overlap and that lie at most max_depth_m apart across (the wall's frames, sills and faces), plus short lines within join_m of the group (sill ends). Opening: along the group's direction, from the median start to the median end of its parallel lines (a window board that sticks out past the opening does not widen it); across, the middle between its outermost lines that start and end within edge_tol_m of the opening's edges. Openings narrower than min_width_m are left out. Wall pieces: wall segments running the same way that end within wall_tol_m of the opening's edges inside its depth. Rooms: probe points from the opening's middle on both sides, beyond its depth, at the side_probe_m distances (the first that finds a room wins).

walls.note: A wall segment runs along a room when at least min_overlap_share of its length lies within room_tol_m of the room's outline.

render.note: Each storey is drawn on a page of its model extent plus margin_m on every side, at 1:scale_1_to (page mm = model mm / scale_1_to). The symbols are sized in mm on that page.
